correctness.rationale: Exact scalar zero-order-held flow yields iid M(H) multipliers with finite log moment; renewal SLLN gives the sample-time exponent and an intersample e^{aH} envelope gives full-time limsup. For k<=a the log gain is nonnegative. For k>a, Y=e^{-aH} has Beta(alpha,1) law. A differentiated beta logarithmic potential has globally positive derivative for alpha<=1/2 by the principal-value cotangent identity; for alpha>1/2 its small-theta coefficient is negative (with separate alpha=1 and alpha>1 boundary expansions). Therefore iff lambda>a/2. Independent finite rational and numerical tests are corroboration, not a universal proof. The ordinary full-time log limit is NOT claimed at zero crossings.

originality.rationale: Compared the literal scalar sample multiplier and the exact gain-existence implication rather than matching titles. The 2018 scalar Poisson paper already proves the mean-square frontier and is credited; its Proposition 6.2 does not assert the pathwise frontier lambda>a/2. The 2022/2023 Poisson papers address mean-exponential control and output regulation. Beutler 1972 supplies a general log-stability theorem but the abstract does not state this sharp intensity threshold; full text unavailable creates a material residual priority risk. Actual mathematical-record searches did not return covering claims. The new threshold requires a nontrivial global sign argument for a singular beta logarithmic potential.

value.rationale: The exact gain-existence threshold for a.s. exponential stabilization is a physically meaningful controller-reliability boundary. It differs by a factor four from the ALREADY-KNOWN mean-square threshold for the IDENTICAL scalar plant: in the intervening open interval a designer can obtain pathwise stabilization without mean-square guarantees. Universal no-gain obstruction at/below the boundary and a constructive near-cancellation gain above it add structural content beyond restating a generic log Lyapunov criterion.
